title: The Developed Runner · 2026

authority.rule: The athlete's authored block, weeks and immutable session versions are the prescription source of truth. This JSON is a web projection and must not independently revise the athlete.

objective: Build a visibly stronger, more substantial runner by expanding the upper frame—lat width, lateral and rear delts, modest upper-trap/neck-frame density, upper-chest depth and arm girth—while adding useful thigh/hamstring girth, preserving a narrow waist, and keeping Adrian light, elastic and fast.
primary_constraint: Running quality remains intact. Strength supports the runner; it never earns the right to degrade the run week.
principle: More specificity, not more punishment. Upper-body development may progress faster; lower-body progression is earned by a normal following run.
running_coordination: The running plan remains owned by Adrian's running coach. This strength plan does not replace, move or invent run workouts. When running load, race demands or recovery conflict with strength, the strength dose yields first.

current_state.label: Week 04 active · physique audit redirected frame work

marathon.evidence: Official race result supplied by athlete/coach

baseline.physique_observation: Very lean, narrow-waisted runner frame with a long neck; calves are already visually prominent and glutes are comparatively developed. Highest-value aesthetic returns are lat width, lateral/rear-delt roundness, modest upper-trap density, upper-chest depth and upper-arm girth. Legs should still gain useful thigh/hamstring density, but direct calf work is maintenance rather than a growth target.
baseline.evidence_limit: No body-mass trend, circumference change or hypertrophy result is claimed until measured.

race_anchors.role: main event / next major marathon after Chapter 01

publication.rule: Public evidence stays bounded to what is measured, reported, observed or officially resulted. Missing evidence stays visible as pending.

measurement_protocol.photos: Every 2 weeks: front relaxed, side relaxed, back relaxed, front lightly flexed; same location, distance, lighting and similar shorts; no pump when possible.
measurement_protocol.body_mass: 3–4 morning measurements per week under similar conditions; use weekly average.
measurement_protocol.strength_evidence: Record actual load and reps on representative anchor movements.

progression_rules: No grinders and no failure. Most lower-body compound work stays around 2 clean reps in reserve.
Upper-body hypertrophy work may approach 1–2 reps in reserve when recovery is normal.
Progress reps inside the range before adding load; then add the smallest practical load and keep execution clean.
Do not add lower-body sets merely because Adrian is disciplined or the calendar advanced.
If lower-body work makes the next run meaningfully heavy, alters mechanics or creates persistent soreness, hold or reduce the lower-body dose before progressing.
If grip or setup limits a lower-body movement before the target tissue does, change the loading setup rather than forcing heavier dumbbells.
Record the work and the run response. Missing evidence stays missing.
A displaced long run or recovery disruption can move or remove a strength session; missed work is not stacked merely to preserve session count.
Race weeks reduce lower-body volume and eccentric cost before touching upper-frame development.
Direct calf work is maintenance only. Skip it when the calves are tender; running already supplies substantial lower-leg loading.
Rear-delt and lat work may receive a second weekly exposure when shoulder and running recovery are normal.
Upper-trap work stays modest: enough to frame Adrian's long neck, not enough to turn the block into shrug specialization.

phases.name: Establish
phases.intent: Find the tolerable dose, then redirect it. Nothing is pushed while the body learns to be loaded at all.

phases.name: Density
phases.intent: Expand the frame: lats, lateral/rear delts, upper chest, arms and modest upper traps. Keep thigh/hamstring girth moving; calves are maintenance.

phases.name: Absorb
phases.intent: Absorb the development block into the 10K while preserving frame work and reducing lower-body cost.

phases.name: Rebuild
phases.intent: Rebuild frame and leg density between races, then quiet the legs for the half.

phases.name: Close
phases.intent: Return to the highest-value frame + thigh dose, then close the year with measurements and low fatigue.

weeks.name: Baseline
weeks.intent: Find repeatable loads. Learn the dose. Finish every session able to train again.

weeks.name: Redirect
weeks.intent: Keep the proven four-day rhythm, but spend the recovery budget where Adrian has the most useful room to develop.
weeks.progression_note: Known run structure: Wednesday quality and Saturday long run are protected. Do not make up the missed Sunday lift. Upper A may move one day if recovery is normal. Lower work stays controlled and yields if the run response is not normal.

run_context.prior_day_context: The prior long run shifted from Saturday to Sunday. The planned Sunday strength session was skipped, and the athlete reported reduced recovery from travel and a late return.
run_context.strength_adjustment: Do not make up or compress missed strength. Upper A may move from Monday to Tuesday after the easy run and strides if recovery is normal. Thursday Lower A stays controlled. Friday Upper B stays as written. Sunday Lower B is conditional on normal legs after Saturday; otherwise it is skipped rather than rolled forward.

weeks.name: Confirm
weeks.intent: Confirm the redirected Week 02 menu inside the 48-mile run week. Do not add lower-body volume.
weeks.progression_note: Repeat the Week 02 architecture. Upper-body reps/load may move when clean. Lower-body progression requires normal running; hold the dose if the mileage increase is already the progression.

weeks.name: Density
weeks.intent: Begin the first true development block: denser torso, arms, medial thigh, hamstrings and lower leg with bounded lower-body fatigue.
weeks.progression_note: Physique audit redirect: frame width and rear shoulder development move up; calves come out this week while tenderness settles. Leg-girth work stays intact. Upper-body progression remains clean, not maximal.

weeks.name: 10K Integration
weeks.intent: Keep strength present while the November 15 10K approaches. No late lower-body accumulation.

weeks.name: 10K Race Week
weeks.intent: Arrive at the 10K with strength maintained and lower-body fatigue low.
weeks.progression_note: Three strength exposures only. Tuesday lower work is a primer, not a workout to win. No lower lifting after Tuesday; Sunday is the race.

weeks.name: Restore
weeks.intent: Absorb the 10K, restore normal movement and return to development without a rebound volume spike.
weeks.progression_note: Three sessions. Resume normal loading only when the legs feel normal after the race.

weeks.intent: Maintain strength and arrive at the December 6 half with quiet legs.

weeks.name: Restore + Read
weeks.intent: Recover from the half, review the running response and re-enter normal strength without forcing the calendar.
weeks.progression_note: Three sessions. If the half was treated harder than planned, hold lower loading. This week is for information, not proving toughness.

weeks.name: Build
weeks.intent: Return to the most productive development dose of the season with running still governing lower-body progression.
weeks.progression_note: Upper body can push progression. Lower body stays compact, strong and repeatable. Keep glute work at maintenance while chest, arms, medial thigh, hamstrings and calves remain the visual priorities.

weeks.name: Build Heavy
weeks.intent: Progress the year-end build by reps or the smallest load increase while keeping the running feel recognizable.
weeks.progression_note: No new movements. Beat Week 14 only where the evidence says to. Do not use holiday schedule disruption as a reason to cram missed work.

weeks.name: Closeout
weeks.intent: Close the 2026 study block with low fatigue, measurements and a clear record for January.
weeks.progression_note: Two sessions only. No failure, no testing. Complete standardized photos, body-mass average and circumferences before January starts fresh.

aesthetic_hierarchy.source: coach photo audit + Oct 5 repeat tape checkpoint
priority: modest upper traps to frame the long neck
rules: Frame width is the highest-return visual change because the waist is already 31 inches.
Rear delts get two weekly exposures in productive upper weeks.
Upper traps get a small weekly dose; no direct neck flexion/extension work is required.
Leg girth remains a real goal. Lower-body work is not reduced to runner-only maintenance, but it must remain compatible with key runs.
Calves are already visually developed. Direct calf hypertrophy is reduced; acute tenderness overrides calf loading.

revision.performance_horizon: Athlete-reported ~2:40 marathon remains a long-term horizon; running quality still governs lower-body progression.
